csv_project_name: Consultant for Water Park Feasibility Study
csv_scope_of_work: Augusta, Georgia, is soliciting statement of proposals from qualified firms to provide professional consulting services a Water Park Feasibility Study for August Recreation and Parks Department. Augusta-Richmond County is evaluating the feasibility of developing a public-private water park facility to enhance recreation, tourism, and economic development. Augusta-Richmond County will be contributing up to $5,000,000 in seed money along with property for the development. Augusta is now seeking a qualified firm to perform a feasibility study for this project. The selected proposer will have demonstrated experience in performing similar studies resulting in successful projects, significant expertise in attraction development and financial modelling, and a strong plan for performance of the study.
csv_disciplines_requested: Architecture Services, Landscape Architecture, Civil Engineering, Feasibility Studies, Planning/Master Planning, Hydrology/Hydraulics

title: Consultant for Water Park Feasibility Study
short_description: Feasibility study for a proposed public-private water park in Augusta, Georgia.
project_scope: Feasibility study for development of a public-private water park facility for Augusta-Richmond County Recreation and Parks Department. The county plans to contribute up to 5000000 USD in seed funding plus property for the development. No technical dimensions, gross floor area, or structural spans are stated.
services: Professional consulting services for a water park feasibility study, including attraction development expertise, financial modelling, and planning for study performance; disciplines requested include architecture, landscape architecture, civil engineering, feasibility studies, planning/master planning, and hydrology/hydraulics.
relevance_explanation:
- This is a feasibility study only, not a structural or detailed planning assignment.
- The project is a water park/leisure development, not a bridge, long-span roof, stadium, or special structure clearly aligned with sbp's core profile.
- Requested services emphasize feasibility, attraction development, and financial modelling rather than structural engineering.
- The brief lacks technical information on notable spans, complex structures, or innovative lightweight construction.
- Feasibility studies are explicitly low-priority compared with direct engineering design opportunities.
construction_cost_explanation: The tender states Augusta-Richmond County will contribute up to 5000000 USD in seed money plus property for the development. This is not necessarily the total construction cost, but it is the only explicit cost figure provided.
fee_explanation: No design fee or consulting fee is stated. The notice is for a feasibility study only, with no basis to derive a reliable sbp fee estimate from the provided information.
references_qualifications: Qualified firms must demonstrate experience performing similar feasibility studies resulting in successful projects, significant expertise in attraction development and financial modelling, and a strong plan for performance of the study.
award_criteria: Not explicitly stated; the notice indicates evaluation will consider relevant similar-study experience, expertise in attraction development and financial modelling, and the proposed plan for performing the study.
contracting_authority: Augusta-Richmond County Consolidated Government, 535 Telfair Street, Suite 605, Augusta, GA 30901, USA. Contact: Tywanna Scott. Email: procbidandcontract@augustaga.gov. Phone: 706-821-2422. Website: https://ssl.doas.state.ga.us/gpr/eventDetails?eSourceNumber=PE-72155-NONST-2026-000000189&sourceSystemType=gpr20
notes: Project Number: 26-905. Mandatory virtual pre-submittal meeting on 06/01/2026 at 11:00 AM EDT via Microsoft Teams. Questions due 06/02/2026 05:00 PM EDT. Although categorized here as Sports due to the water park program, the procurement is primarily a feasibility/planning study and not a direct structural design opportunity.
